prediction_ref.short_label: Token-drift trajectory probes land as agentic-coherence audit primitive by Q4 2026

validation_rows.evidence_summary: Today's own prediction lands directly on the Thursday CMU Catalyst plus Meta FAIR ArXiv submission at arxiv.org/abs/2605.11823 titled 'Token-Drift Trajectories: A Causal Probe for Long-Horizon Agentic Coherence Failures' by CMU Catalyst PhD candidate Tianqi Chen, Meta FAIR senior research scientist Naman Goyal, and Catalyst lab director Zhihao Jia. The paper is the first publication to extend the Stanford CRFM plus DeepMind reservoir-routing line from Wednesday's arxiv 2605.10142 by characterizing the failure-mode side of long-horizon agentic inference rather than the routing-side optimization, introducing a probe instrument the authors call 'token-drift trajectory mapping' that traces how the expert-selection sequence diverges from the intended task-policy distribution over multi-turn agentic conversations. On the same 145B-parameter MoE backbone used in reservoir routing, token drift accumulates super-linearly past 12 tool-use turns and a simple drift-magnitude threshold at the policy-divergence inflection predicts SWE-Bench Verified failure modes with 84.3 percent accuracy. The paper's proposed 'drift-aware checkpoint' primitive composes additively with reservoir routing rather than replacing it, lifting the reservoir-routing-augmented backbone from 78.7 to 81.2 on SWE-Bench Verified (a fresh 2.5pp absolute lift on top of Wednesday's reservoir-routing uplift) while reducing per-turn router-compute cost by an additional 12.8 percent on the same 8x H100 SXM5 reference node. Simon Willison flagged the paper as the second credible MoE-router primitive shipping inside 48 hours and the first composition demonstration the agentic-MoE routing-space optimization line has produced; Hacker News surfaced two independent reproductions on CoreWeave H100 SXM5 rentals inside the same Thursday window with throughput numbers landing inside 2.8 percent of the CMU-Meta reference sheet.
